reply.rationale: No defensible compositional paradigm survives the evidence tests. The numbered S1–S14 and P1–P14 forms fail the opaque-index test: the numerals do not contribute a stable literal meaning such as count, duration, or ordered semantic contrast across a shared frame; instead each whole form names an idiosyncratic symptom or procedure. The candidate splits based on shared prefixes/suffixes (S1-, P1-, -10, -11, etc.) are unsupported because the residues do not form a meaning-consistent substitution class in a common construction. Other surface resemblances such as bright/right or CC/C likewise lack a stable compositional contrast. Although the codebook includes standalone semantic key entries for faces and intensities, there is no independently supported multi-morpheme construction in which those values alternate, so they remain lexical symbols here rather than paradigm members. Therefore the safest complete partition is a flat lexicon.
